scope: Prevent DXF output from silently omitting LOFTEDSURFACE DWG cross-section and guide-curve references while retaining the already-modeled DXF token pass-through path.

research.pathCurve: The prior path-curve receipt records that Autodesk's Lofted Surface DXF field table has no group-5 path-reference field. The ordinary entity group 5 remains reserved for the surface identity.

peerCrosswalk.mapping: HANDLE_VECTOR cross_sections and guide_curves to repeated DXF group 310; path_curve has DXF code 0.
peerCrosswalk.writer: src/out_dxf.c formats vector handle values as group-310 text, while libdxfrw's existing DXF model retains group-90 integers and group-310 byte chunks as opaque DRW_Variant values.

research.localGap: libdxfrw's DWG parser retains crossSectionHandles, guideCurveHandles, numCrossSections, and numGuideCurves. The DXF writer emits only dxfReferenceData and has no verified handle-to-group-310 byte encoding, source-to-output remapping, or dependency-closure path for these DWG fields.

implementation.behavior: writeSurface now refuses nonzero cross-section/guide counts and nonempty corresponding DWG handle vectors before publishing the entity record. The existing nonzero pathCurveHandle refusal remains. DXF-origin dxfReferenceData group-90/group-310 tokens continue through the existing bounded writer unchanged.
implementation.compatibility: The DWG writer is unchanged. The DXF pass-through path for captured group-90/group-310 tokens is unchanged. Only unsupported DWG-origin reference projections are refused.
implementation.failureBehavior: ASCII and Binary output preserve the preexisting destination prefix on each refusal. A valid DXF-token profile writes to a separate writer and retains the ordinary entity group-5 identity.

validation.positiveProfile: Captured group-90 integer and group-310 bytes are emitted; output contains only the surface's normal group-5 identity.

limits: No physical LOFTEDSURFACE DWG/DXF pair was added or converted.
The peer schema mapping does not by itself establish Autodesk's semantic contract or native-consumer behavior.
No handle remapping, target uniqueness, ownership, closure, or native CAD readback is established for group-310 references.
The surface's ACIS payload and geometric meaning remain outside this control.
next: If enabling DWG-origin group-310 projection is pursued, establish exact byte encoding and remap behavior from a traceable producer pair, validate every target role and graph edge, and require ASCII/Binary typed readback plus a native consumer check. Until then retain the atomic refusal.
